title: Chicken Lo Mein with Pak Choi and Shiitake
summary: Tender egg noodles are tossed with chicken, shiitake mushrooms and pak choi in a glossy soy and oyster sauce.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large non-stick frying pan (30 cm)
small bowls for the prepared ingredients

ingredients.item: skinless chicken breast or thigh, thinly sliced
pak choi, stems sliced, leaves halved
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Bring 3 litres of unsalted water to the boil and cook the noodles for 2-3 minutes until just tender with a little bite left. Drain and rinse briefly under warm water to wash off the surface starch, then shake dry and toss with the sesame oil. Unlike chow mein noodles, these are tossed rather than fried, so they need to be fully cooked through before they go anywhere near the wok.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Toss the sliced chicken with the soy sauce and cornflour and set aside while you prepare everything else. The cornflour forms a thin protective coating that keeps the meat juicy through the quick high-heat stir-fry.

steps.title: Whisk the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together the oyster sauce, light and dark soy sauces, sugar, stock and cornflour in a jug. Keep it by the stove, as the cornflour will settle and need a quick whisk again before it's poured in.

steps.title: Stir-fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 3-4 minutes until golden with no pink remaining — check the thickest piece reaches 74°C. Lift it out and set aside.

steps.title: Stir-fry mushrooms and carrot
steps.text: Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the shiitake and carrot for 2 minutes, until the mushrooms pick up some colour. Mushrooms release moisture as they cook, so letting them sit and colour rather than stirring constantly helps that liquid cook off instead of pooling.

steps.title: Add aromatics and pak choi
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger and pak choi stems for 1 minute, then add the leaves for a final 30 seconds. The stems need the extra minute to soften, while the leaves wilt almost instantly and go limp and watery if left too long.

steps.title: Toss noodles into the sauce
steps.text: Add the noodles, chicken and sauce to the wok and toss everything together with tongs for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly and clings to every strand.

steps.title: Finish with spring onion
steps.text: Scatter over the spring onions, toss once more and serve straight away while the noodles are hot and glossy.

tips: Cook the noodles until fully tender before tossing, since lo mein noodles aren't fried afterwards the way chow mein noodles are — undercooked ones will stay chewy.
Let the mushrooms sit for a moment rather than stirring constantly, so the liquid they release cooks away instead of leaving the stir-fry watery.
Add the pak choi leaves right at the end — they wilt in seconds and go limp and watery if they cook alongside the stems.
safety: Check the chicken's thickest piece reaches 74°C with no pink before setting it aside.
storage: Keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot wok or microwave, stirring in a splash of water, until piping hot throughout (at least 74°C). Freezing isn't recommended, as the pak choi and noodles turn soft and watery once thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
